title: olyan barát, aki...: Describing a Friend with aki

sections.title: Describing a person by what they do
sections.content: You know *aki* from A2 (Unit 4). To describe a friend in more than one adjective, Hungarian often reaches for a relative clause built with *aki* ("who"): *olyan barátom van, aki mindig meghallgat*, "I have a friend who always listens to me." *olyan* ("such a/a certain kind of") signals that a description is coming, and *aki* then introduces the clause that supplies it. This lets you combine an adjective like *őszinte* or *hűséges* with a whole action, not just a single word.

items.spanish: Van egy őszinte barátom, aki mindig megmondja az igazat.
items.english: I have an honest friend who always tells the truth.

items.spanish: Olyan hűséges barátom van, aki sosem hagy cserben.
items.english: I have the kind of loyal friend who never lets me down.

items.spanish: Önzetlen barátra van szükségem, aki mindig segít.
items.english: I need a selfless friend who always helps.

sections.content: *aki* is the subject of its own clause, whatever the case of the noun before it: *barátra van szükségem, aki mindig segít* (*barátra* has *-ra*, *aki* stays *aki*). Forms like *akire* or *akivel* come later in B1 (Unit 21).
